summary: Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under guide V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodoor Paul Galestin (1907–1987) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom around 1930 to 1936 and was appointed professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University in 1957.

Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his dissertation at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1843–1847). He served as Privatdozent at Berlin (1850), worked at the Bodleian Library (1852), and held professorships at Edinburgh (1861–1875) and Bonn (1875–1889).

Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Munich and the University of Göttingen, completing his Ph.D. (~1828) and Habilitation (~1834). At Göttingen, he served as Privatdozent (1834), Lehrmeister (1848), and Ordinarius (1862–1881).

Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch (~1888–1892) and continued his studies under Georg Bühler (~1892–1895).

Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Königsberg, Bonn, and Paris under von Bohlen, Rosenkranz, Lassen, and Burnouf. He served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London and University of London from 1851 to 1872.

Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) was a linguist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studies at Göttingen, Vienna, Leiden, and Berlin, he held posts at Göttingen, Kiel University (1864, 1868–1872), and the University of Strasbourg (1872–1906).

Theodor Zachariae (1851–1934) was an Indologist. He earned his PhD at Göttingen (~1874) and his Habilitation at Greifswald (~1879), studying under Sauppe, Curtius, Brockhaus, and Benfey. He held professorships at Greifswald (1883) and Halle-Wittenberg (1890–1921).

Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) studied at Hopkins School, Yale College, Yale University, and Princeton University. He served as president of Yale University from 1831 to 1871 and president of the American Oriental Society from around 1861 to 1881.

Theodore Riccardi Jr. (1937–) is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He served on the faculty at Columbia University (attested 2014), where he is attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.
Theophil Gubler was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Basel under Jacob Wackernagel, completing his doctoral degree by 1903.
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Chicago and is attested as Vertretungsprofessor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).

Thierry Mathou (1963–) is a political scientist and Tibetology scholar. Educated at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, he held posts at the National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) as an Associated Political Scientist.

Thierry Meynard (1963–) is a philosopher and sinologist. He earned his PhD in philosophy at Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003), became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006), and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis R. Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and was Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje), and later founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. under Paul J. Griffiths), and served as associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed (1954–) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~1981–1989) under William R. Hutchison, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).
